folders.reason: DTED height data (levels 0 to 2) for viewsheds

groups.label: Height data
groups.description: Where the DTED height data is, and how much memory the parsed cells may use.

groups.label: Viewshed and height map
groups.description: How viewsheds and height maps are computed, and the limits on one request.

heightDataFolder.title: Height data folder
heightDataFolder.description: The folder with the DTED height data: one file per cell, e<lon>/n<lat>.dt0, .dt1 or .dt2 (a w or s for west and south). Either an absolute path (for example shared storage), or a path below the emcc folder that starts with %emcc%/ (ECore resolves it; one that leaves the emcc folder is refused). Empty: not set. The value reaches every logged-in browser.

x-emc2.hint: DTED cells: an absolute path, or one under %emcc%/; empty: not set

refractionCoefficient.title: Refraction coefficient
refractionCoefficient.description: The atmospheric refraction coefficient k of the line of sight: a height at distance d is lowered by d squared over twice the earth's radius, times (1 - k).

x-emc2.hint: k in the line of sight's curvature term, 0 to 1

maxRange.title: Longest range
maxRange.description: The longest range a viewshed may have, and the largest radius of a height map circle, in metres.

x-emc2.hint: The longest viewshed range and the largest height map radius

maxCells.title: Most height cells per request
maxCells.description: The most height cells (grid points) one viewshed or height map may need within its range. A finer level that needs more is replaced by a coarser one; when none fits, the request is refused.

x-emc2.hint: The most height cells one request may need; a coarser level, else refused

timeoutSeconds.title: Request timeout
timeoutSeconds.description: How long a viewshed or height map may take, reading the data included, before it is refused.

x-emc2.hint: How long a request may take, reading the data included

cacheMegabytes.title: Height cell cache
cacheMegabytes.description: The memory the parsed height cells may use together; the least recently used go first.

x-emc2.hint: Memory for the parsed height cells; the least recently used go first
